patches.text: 6. **Other-income concentration.** Q2 OI Rs 6.98 Cr vs Q1 Rs 7.33 Cr: flat, not spiking. OI share of PBT fell from 47.7% to 15.5% YoY. Market gains are Rs 4.43 Cr, 31.0%: MTM gain Rs 1.96 Cr (l.634) and investment-sale gain Rs 2.47 Cr (l.638). One-offs are Rs 2.35 Cr, 16.4%: lease-modification gain Rs 0.94 Cr (l.635) and unrealised FX gain Rs 1.41 Cr (l.628). Provision write-back Rs 0.10 Cr (l.636) and PPE sale gain Rs 0.03 Cr (l.637) are small. Rs 3.71 Cr (25.9%) is not named. The FX and lease gains sit in PBT (filed); their placement inside the OI line is [INFERENCE]. So market gains and one-offs, not treasury yield, carry the "steady run rate" (call l.319-321). Q2 split ND (the cash flow is H1 only).

The one number that could flip the organic read is the ASR 'Hobel 30% of H1': at that level organic revenue fell QoQ; at Hobel's FY26 run-rate it grew. Two A3 items were resolved from supporting documents: the Saudi ODI could not be IPO-funded (proceeds 100% used by 30-Sep), and the CARE report's total row does not add. CRISIL is a non-disclosure, not an evasion; no analyst asked. Credibility is C on one scored call, so the grade is fragile."
